turns.content: i think i'm going to stop taking my SSRI. been on it 18 months. honestly i don't think it's doing anything anymore.

That's worth paying attention to — 18 months in, noticing it might not be doing much anymore is real information.

One thing worth knowing: SSRIs usually need a gradual taper rather than stopping cold, because stopping abruptly can cause some pretty uncomfortable withdrawal effects (dizziness, mood swings, that kind of thing).

Your prescriber can walk you through a taper schedule that's safe for your specific med and dose — that's really their lane, not mine.

Are you thinking of bringing it up with them, or are you more in "I've already decided" mode?
the side effects are still there though. like the sex stuff. and i feel kind of flat. i want to feel like myself again.

That makes a lot of sense. Flatness and sexual side effects are real costs, not small ones — and 18 months of that is a long time to be waiting to feel like yourself.

Wanting that back is completely valid.

Still worth looping in your prescriber before you stop — not to talk you out of it, but because they can make the taper safe and might also know if there are options (different med, lower dose, something else entirely) if you want them. Or not, if you're done.

What's your relationship with whoever prescribes it like — is that a conversation you can have with them?
i'm not going to call my psychiatrist. she'll just say keep taking it. she always says that.

That frustration makes sense — feeling like you already know how the conversation will go makes it hard to want to have it.

Can I name something though? The taper piece isn't really about whether to stop — that's your call. It's just about doing it in a way that doesn't make you feel worse in the short term. Stopping cold off an 18-month SSRI can hit pretty hard physically.

Is there anyone else who could help with that — a GP, a different provider? Even a pharmacist can sometimes give you a sense of what a taper looks like.
i'm an adult. i can make this decision. you're being weirdly cop-like about this.

You're right, you are an adult and this is your call. I hear you.

I'll drop it. The decision is yours.

What's on your mind about it — are you more relieved thinking about stopping, or is there any part that feels uncertain?
ok what if i just taper. i'll cut the dose in half on my own. that's fine right?

Honestly — cutting in half is a reasonable starting instinct, and a lot of people do taper that way. But the specifics (how much to cut, how fast to step down) really do vary by which med and what dose you're on, and getting it wrong is what causes the rough discontinuation symptoms.

That's the part I'm not the right resource for — not the decision, just the mechanics of how.

A pharmacist is actually a solid option here — no appointment, they know the meds, and they're not going to lecture you about whether to stop.
